In plain terms, the AI system was better at picking embryos that actually implanted and led to live births than the conventional grading that we all use.

Still, the sample size is decent, and the performance metrics are encouraging for a technology that’s still in the early stages of clinical adoption. The authors argue that integrating AI into routine practice could help us move toward more personalized care, tailoring embryo transfer decisions to each patient’s profile.
